description: The true path of the miniature: one shot told at two times by two honest witnesses, each by a clock; the slow clock found, the gardener's time set aside, and with it the alibi.

moves.see: counted the strokes of the hall clock
moves.why: Susan counted nine strokes of the hall clock as the shot came.

moves.see: he left the library at ten to nine
moves.why: Mr. Royle left me at ten to nine by the hall clock.

moves.see: the hall clock was right that evening
moves.why: I set the hall clock myself that morning, by the church.
Bowker took his time from the stable clock.

moves.see: his quarter to nine was nine
moves.why: And the stable clock is a quarter of an hour slow.
So the shot was not at a quarter to nine: that was the stable clock's time, not the true one.
Bowker told me what he saw; it was the clock that was wrong.
Both clocks, read right, say nine.
The shot came at nine by the hall clock, the clock he left me by.
He had been gone ten minutes.
Only if the slow clock were right.
